headline: The biggest adjustment is switching from relaxed, touch-friendly Filipino habits to Saudi restraint: right-hand-only dining, no public affection, and careful gestures around elders and the opposite gender.

watch_outs.title: Right hand only for food
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos eat with fork and spoon in either hand, and left-hand use is rarely noticed.
watch_outs.to_norm: In Saudi Arabia the left hand is reserved for hygiene; eat, pass food, and hand over money with the right hand only.
watch_outs.do: Keep your left hand in your lap and use your right for every bite and every handover.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not hold bread, pass a dish, or hand cash with your left hand.

watch_outs.title: No public affection at all
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipino couples hold hands and share brief cheek touches in public, especially in cities.
watch_outs.to_norm: Public displays of affection are illegal under Saudi decency law, even for married couples.
watch_outs.do: Keep all physical affection, including long hand-holding, for private spaces.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not hug, kiss, or hold hands with a partner in malls, restaurants, or streets.

watch_outs.title: Feet flat, never soles toward others
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos treat foot position as a minor faux pas and rarely think about it day to day.
watch_outs.to_norm: In Saudi Arabia showing the soles of your feet is rude; keep feet flat or crossed at the ankles.
watch_outs.do: Sit with both feet on the floor and tuck them away when sitting on floor cushions.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not cross an ankle over your knee or point a foot toward anyone.

watch_outs.title: Greet opposite gender cautiously
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipino cheek-to-cheek greetings are common with friends and family of either gender.
watch_outs.to_norm: In Saudi Arabia cheek-kissing is common between men but not across genders; with women, default to a verbal greeting.
watch_outs.do: Greet with words and a nod, and offer a hand only if the other person extends first.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not lean in for a cheek touch or extend your hand to a Saudi woman unless she offers hers.

watch_outs.title: Accept host food and coffee
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos hesitate then accept a small token portion, and can decline politely if full.
watch_outs.to_norm: Refusing a Saudi host's coffee or food is rude; accept the first offer and shake the cup lightly to signal enough.
watch_outs.do: Take the first cup or plate offered, and shake the cup gently when returning it to stop refills.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not say no outright to the first offer of coffee, dates, or a meal.

watch_outs.title: Shoes off, prayer rug respected
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos commonly remove shoes at home but often keep them on in some households.
watch_outs.to_norm: Shoes are expected off in most Saudi homes, and a prayer rug must never be stepped on with shoes.
watch_outs.do: Watch your host at the entrance and remove your shoes before stepping inside.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not walk across a prayer rug or into a carpeted sitting room with shoes on.

watch_outs.title: Point with open hand, not finger
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos avoid pointing at people but use a regular index finger for objects and directions.
watch_outs.to_norm: In Saudi Arabia single-finger pointing is avoided; gesture with a whole open hand.
watch_outs.do: Indicate people and things with an open palm and all fingers.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not jab a single index finger at a person or across a room.

watch_outs.title: Skip thumbs-up with elders
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos use the thumbs-up freely as a friendly sign of approval.
watch_outs.to_norm: In Saudi formal and religious settings the thumbs-up has shifted meaning; use words instead with elders.
watch_outs.do: Say a verbal 'tamam' or 'good' when agreeing with senior colleagues or officials.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not flash a thumbs-up to an elder, a sheikh, or in a mosque setting.

watch_outs.title: Modest dress, no shorts
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos wear shorts, sleeveless tops, and casual wear freely in malls and streets.
watch_outs.to_norm: Saudi public dress is modest; men avoid sleeveless tops and short shorts, women wear loose covering clothing.
watch_outs.do: Pack loose long trousers and long-sleeved tops, and carry a light scarf or abaya for conservative areas.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not wear shorts, tank tops, or tight or revealing clothing in public.

watch_outs.title: Punctuality in business, patience in waits
watch_outs.from_norm: Filipinos treat 'Filipino time' as fine socially but aim to be on time for business.
watch_outs.to_norm: Saudi meetings expect you to arrive on time, but hosts may keep you waiting without it being an insult.
watch_outs.do: Arrive on time or early and wait calmly, using the time for small talk.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not show irritation or leave because a Saudi counterpart is late.
